correctness.rationale: For real finite-dimensional SPD A and B, C=I+hB/2 and T=I-h A C^-1, direct noncommutative expansion gives C(I-T^T T)C=h(2A+hK), K=(A(B-A)+(B-A)A)/2. Thus Euclidean nonexpansivity is equivalent to 2A+hK positive semidefinite; no commutativity is presumed. When B=A+vv^T, S=A^-1/2 K A^-1/2=(ab^T+ba^T)/2 with a=A^1/2 v,b=A^-1/2 v has nonzero eigenvalues (s ± sqrt(alpha beta))/2. Strict Cauchy-Schwarz gives delta=sqrt(alpha beta)-s>0 iff Av is not parallel to v, so h*=4/delta is the inclusive sharp one-step norm boundary. Alignment gives positive definite 2A+hK for all h>0. A second exact congruence C(A^-1-T^T A^-1 T)C=h(2I+h vv^T) is positive definite, and h C^-1/2 A C^-1/2 has eigenvalues in (0,2) because B>=A>0, establishing weighted strict contraction and spectrum in (-1,1) even for h>h*. Exact rational witness A=diag(1,4), v=(1,1) has h*=8 and h=16 ratio 1557/1301; independent exact congruences checked 12 matrix cases.
